profile.reading: This data center in Mantsala, Finland, about 40 to 60 kilometers north of Helsinki depending on the source, was built by Yandex on land the company purchased in 2013, described by Yandex at the time as its first greenfield, purpose built data center project, distinct from Googles nearby Hamina facility, which really was converted from a former paper mill; sources differ on this Mantsala buildings own opening date, with one directory citing 2014 and Finnish and trade press coverage citing operational since 2015, recorded here with that conflict noted honestly. The building uses a distinctive aerodynamic sloped roof designed to help direct cool outside air into its ventilation system, and recovers waste server heat for the local district heating network, with roughly 20,000 megawatt hours a year of heat recovery reported and power usage effectiveness as low as 1.1. Reported IT capacity figures also vary by period, with an earlier 2010s account citing roughly 20 megawatts against Googles 80 megawatt Hamina site at the time, while more recent 2024 through 2026 listings describe 24 to 25 megawatts currently operating with an active expansion toward a targeted 75 megawatts and plans involving tens of thousands of GPUs; this registry records the more recent operating figure as it_capacity_mw and the expansion target as planned_it_capacity_mw. Finland was chosen in part for political and economic stability, reliable and comparatively inexpensive electricity, and a cold climate supporting free air cooling. Critically, this facilitys ownership has changed since the operator name on this record was set: Yandex N.V., the Dutch parent company, completed the sale of its Russian business to a consortium of investors over the winter of 2023 to 2024, and its remaining international and European operations, including this Mantsala site, were rebranded as Nebius Group in 2024. Nebius has publicly stated it acquired or retained the Mantsala facility from Yandex Cloud in August 2024 and now owns and operates the building as part of a European AI infrastructure investment program exceeding 1 billion dollars, and has separately announced plans for a larger new Finland site in Lappeenranta. This registrys operator field still reads Yandex and should be understood as historical, pending a broader operator name correction pass across this record.
